original_test_intent: Install the approved Windows Server image onto the authorized target disk with TPM enabled, CSM disabled and Secure Boot Standard Mode, install the approved device drivers, and prove Secure Boot plus clean normal reboot and firmware/BMC logs.
original_method: Identify dedicated SUT and target disk; preserve backup/recovery keys; verify media checksum, storage driver and SDL set; qualified operator sets the approved BIOS/TPM/Secure Boot state and performs interactive install; collect installer/storage/driver evidence; run elevated Confirm-SecureBootUEFI; verify CSM/Standard Mode, device health, UEFI/BMC logs and a controlled reboot; leave approved final state.
manual_activity: Qualified operator selects the disk, controls BIOS/TPM and Windows setup, loads drivers and runs elevated confirmation; agent may collect read-only inventory and logs.
required_inputs: Approved Windows Server edition/image/checksum and license/install media
Exact target disk/controller and backup/reimage authorization
Approved RAID/storage and full SDL driver versions
Secure Boot/TPM/CSM matrix, recovery keys/media, expected log policy and maintenance approval
safety_requirements: Physically/logically identify the target disk and preserve backup/recovery material
Use approved media/drivers and qualified interactive operator
Preserve pre-test logs rather than erasing evidence; isolate dedicated SUT
Stop on wrong disk, media/driver failure, key/security anomaly or boot/recovery loss; no automatic retry

Capture installer, Confirm-SecureBootUEFI, Device Manager/driver and reboot/log evidence
Verify approved final settings and access after operator actions

Approve TPM/Secure Boot/CSM states and recovery material
Define driver/log/error acceptance and final state
Review evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Linux `bootctl`/`mokutil` can only describe a pre-existing Linux environment and the shown SSH syntax is malformed; it cannot establish the target Windows Secure Boot result.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use firmware evidence plus elevated Windows `Confirm-SecureBootUEFI`, approved Windows device/driver inventory and event/log export after the operator installation.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Windows Server 2012/R2 wording, RAID-driver conditional, SDL drivers, security settings, confirmation, logs and reboot remain; exact supported image and packages are pending.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed-media manifest, explicit disk map, staged driver list and security-state matrix, then capture Windows-native Secure Boot/device/log and reboot evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact destructive target, checksums, recovery and auditable driver/security acceptance without replacing the interactive install.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A pre-install Linux status cannot substitute for the installed Windows result or prove all required drivers and logs are clean.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Installing an obsolete OS may be unsupported by current hardware or Secure Boot policy; engineering must approve the exact edition/build rather than silently modernize it.

project_override_considerations: If Windows Server 2012/R2 is unsupported, record BLOCKED or approve a separate variant; do not substitute a newer OS under this source row. Interpret 'standard UEFI and BMC under OS' only through an approved checklist.
expected_evidence: SUT/disk/controller identity, approval and backup/recovery record
ISO/checksum, storage and SDL driver manifests
Pre/post BIOS TPM Secure Boot CSM evidence
Installer and driver/device results plus Confirm-SecureBootUEFI True
UEFI/BMC/Windows logs, reboot/availability timeline, final state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require a Windows installation with Secure Boot, TPM, drivers, logs and reboot. Ambiguous package/version details are missing engineering inputs rather than contradictory goals.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The workflow remains conditionally executable on a dedicated authorized SUT when the destructive target, media, drivers and recovery inputs are supplied.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2259 Wistron-HW-00244-V004: approve exact Windows Server 2012/R2 edition/build/ISO checksum and platform support, target disk/controller plus backup/reimage authorization, RAID and full SDL driver manifests; approve TPM physical-presence and CSM-disabled/Secure Boot Standard state, recovery keys/media, Windows-native driver/Secure Boot/log acceptance, the meaning of `standard UEFI and BMC under OS`, reboot/final-state requirements and destructive-install supervision.

review_improvement: Preserves all installation and security coverage while preventing an ambiguous precheck from authorizing a wrong-disk wipe or substituting for Windows-native results.
independent_technical_reasoning: OS installation is destructive and the disk selected after loading a RAID driver may not retain the same enumeration seen beforehand. Secure Boot setup also affects accepted boot media and TPM-sealed recovery. The target evidence must therefore bind media checksum, controller/disk identity, installed Windows build, signed driver inventory and firmware security state. Confirm-SecureBootUEFI is meaningful only in the installed Windows environment, while UEFI/BMC logs must be compared against a retained baseline rather than cleared blindly.
